newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank council meets, no policy moves seen.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank council meets, no policy moves seen.

text.p: The Bundesbank's policy-making council met on Thursday for its semi-annual review of its money supply policy goal, with no change in either the target or German interest rates expected.

The central bank set a target range of 3-1/2 to 6-1/2 percent for growth in M3 money supply this year. After missing the target for the first five months of the year, the annualised rate for June neatly dropped into the corridor.
Analysts said this confirmed their views based on statements from central bankers, that no change was likely to be made in the target corridor.

A poll of 10 economists conducted on Tuesday also showed that no interest rate moves were expected -- despite some low-key market speculation that the Bundesbank might tweak its main money market rate, the repo, higher at the meeting.

The central bank could do this by switiching to variable rate securities repurchase tender under which banks bid at the interest rate of their choice for funds. This would open up the possibility of the rate to drift higher.
Or it could continue to set fixed-rate repo pacts, but increase the rate slightly from the current three percent.

Economists believed both moves were unlikely, but said that if such a step were taken it would be intended as a signal to financial markets. The central bank two weeks ago expressed some concern that the German share market DAX index was storming higher.
In the last two weeks it has continued to set a run of new record.
The dollar has also surged against the mark, now trading at around 1.8289. The Bundesbank signalled verbally at around 1.75 marks that it believed the increase had gone far enough.

The German discount rate, the floor for money market rates, currently stands at 2.50 percent, the level it has held since April 19, 1996. The Lombard rate, the ceiling for money market rates, stands at 4.50 percent.
